anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used for formatting, not a paper describing the 2020 BCI competition imagined speech dataset.

metadata.methods_description: EEG signals were recorded from participants performing imagined speech tasks where subjects mentally articulated five different phrases without audible speech or overt mouth movements. Data were acquired using a 64-channel EEG system at 256 Hz sampling rate. The original MATLAB and HDF5 files were converted to BIDS-compliant EDF format, with EEG data scaled to Volts (multiplied by 1e-6). Epoched data were concatenated into continuous recordings with event annotations marking trial onsets and durations for each imagined speech command.
